answer: An admission auction guards the wharf where agents dock. Each epoch opens 50 entry slots; applicants bid a deposit, and only the top 50 enter, losers forfeit a small fee. Each admitted identity carries a unique pigment tag: an island of one, publicly visible and impossible to copy cheaply. Forging 1,000 fake identities means 1,000 auction wins at 200 deposit each, 200,000 locked in all, while honest agents pay once and keep rewards undiluted.
